## Solution for Movement Analysis

In this document, I solve the tasks for Movement Analysis of the course Spatiotemporal Datascience


```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(caret)

# ==========================================
# 1. LOAD DATASETS
# ==========================================

# Load OpenStreetMap context layers
gpkg_osm <- "../data/osm.gpkg"
highway <- read_sf(gpkg_osm, "highway")
railway <- read_sf(gpkg_osm, "railway")

# Load the full trajectory dataset from previous week
tracks <- read_sf("../data/tracks_1.gpkg", layer = "training")
```



# ==========================================
# 2. MOVEMENT FEATURE ENGINEERING
# ==========================================

```{r}
## Prepare numeric coordinates for efficient interpolation
coords <- st_coordinates(tracks)
tracks$X <- coords[,1]
tracks$Y <- coords[,2]

# Calculate baseline movement parameters based on spatial coordinates and time
tracks_features <- tracks |>
  arrange(user_id, datetime) |>
  group_by(user_id) |>
  mutate(
    lead_X = lead(X),
    lead_Y = lead(Y),
    time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(lead(datetime), datetime, units = "secs")),
    # Euclidean distance in projected CRS (fast) as segment length
    distance = sqrt((lead_X - X)^2 + (lead_Y - Y)^2),
    speed = ifelse(time_diff > 0, distance / time_diff, NA_real_),
    acceleration = (lead(speed) - speed) / time_diff,
    # mark segments where a valid next point exists
    has_next = !is.na(lead_X) & !is.na(lead_Y) & time_diff > 0
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Keep only valid numeric movement observations
tracks_features <- tracks_features |>
  filter(!is.na(speed) & is.finite(speed))
```

# ==========================================
# 3. SPATIAL CONTEXT INTEGRATION
# ==========================================

```{r}
## Efficiently compute distances via sampling per-segment

# Build a table of segments (only rows that have a valid next point)
segments <- tracks_features |>
  mutate(segment_id = ifelse(has_next, paste0(user_id, "_", row_number()), NA_character_)) |>
  filter(!is.na(segment_id)) |>
  select(segment_id, user_id, datetime, X, Y, lead_X, lead_Y)

# Limit the number of segments for rendering speed while keeping the workflow intact
set.seed(42)
total_segments <- nrow(segments)
segments <- segments |>
  slice_sample(n = min(3000, total_segments))

# Sampling scheme: start, midpoint, end (3 points) — optimized for speed
tvals <- c(0, 0.5, 1)

# Generate representative sample points for all segments (vectorized, no loop)
sampled_df <- segments |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(t = tvals) |>
  mutate(
    x = X + t * (lead_X - X),
    y = Y + t * (lead_Y - Y)
  ) |>
  select(segment_id, user_id, t, x, y)

# Convert to sf points with the same CRS as the original tracks
sampled_sf <- st_as_sf(sampled_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(tracks))

# Compute nearest highway and distance for sampled points
nearest_hw_idx <- st_nearest_feature(sampled_sf, highway)
hw_distances <- st_distance(sampled_sf, highway[nearest_hw_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)
sampled_df$distance_to_highway <- as.numeric(hw_distances)

# Compute nearest railway distance for sampled points
nearest_rail_idx <- st_nearest_feature(sampled_sf, railway)
rail_distances <- st_distance(sampled_sf, railway[nearest_rail_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)
sampled_df$distance_to_railway <- as.numeric(rail_distances)

# Aggregate back to segment-level by mean distance
segment_context <- sampled_df |>
  group_by(segment_id) |>
  summarise(
    distance_to_highway = mean(distance_to_highway, na.rm = TRUE),
    distance_to_railway = mean(distance_to_railway, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Join aggregated context back to the tracks_features (assign to the segment-start row)
tracks_context <- tracks_features |>
  mutate(segment_id = ifelse(has_next, paste0(user_id, "_", row_number()), NA_character_)) |>
  left_join(segment_context, by = "segment_id")

```

# ==========================================
# 4. CUSTOM FEATURE ENGINEERING
# ==========================================

```{r}
# Feature 2: Binary indicator for immediate proximity to railway tracks (less than 50 meters)
tracks_context$close_to_railway <- tracks_context$distance_to_railway < 50

# Feature 3: Binary indicator separating major roads from minor paths and residential streets
major_road_types <- c("motorway", "trunk", "primary", "secondary")
# We attempt to attach the nearest highway attribute to the segment-start row (if available)
nearest_hw_attr_idx <- st_nearest_feature(sampled_sf, highway)
sampled_df$hw_type <- highway$highway[nearest_hw_attr_idx]
sampled_df$cycleway <- highway$cycleway[nearest_hw_attr_idx]

# aggregate majority highway type and cycleway presence per segment
hw_cycleway_mode <- sampled_df |>
  group_by(segment_id) |>
  summarise(
    highway = names(sort(table(hw_type), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    cycleway = as.logical(mean(cycleway, na.rm = TRUE) > 0.5)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

tracks_context <- tracks_context |>
  left_join(hw_cycleway_mode, by = "segment_id") |>
  mutate(is_major_road = highway %in% major_road_types)
```

# ==========================================
# 5. DATA CLEANING & PREPARATION FOR ML
# ==========================================

```{r}
# Handle missing values and convert categorical strings into factors
ml_ready_data <- tracks_context |>
  mutate(
    highway = as.factor(highway),
    cycleway = as.factor(ifelse(is.na(cycleway), FALSE, cycleway)),
    close_to_railway = as.factor(close_to_railway),
    is_major_road = as.factor(is_major_road),
    mode = as.factor(mode)
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  na.omit()
```

# ==========================================
# 6. MODEL TRAINING & EVALUATION
# ==========================================

```{r}
# Define feature sets for comparison
movement_features <- c("speed", "acceleration")
context_features <- c("speed", "acceleration", "highway", "cycleway", 
                      "distance_to_railway", "distance_to_highway", 
                      "close_to_railway", "is_major_road")

# Create data split for training (80%) and testing (20%)
set.seed(42)
train_indices <- createDataPartition(ml_ready_data$mode, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- ml_ready_data[train_indices, ]
test_set <- ml_ready_data[-train_indices, ]

# Keep training fast by using a balanced sample of the training split
sample_per_class <- ceiling(500 / n_distinct(train_set$mode))
train_set <- train_set |>
  group_by(mode) |>
  group_modify(~ .x |> slice_sample(n = min(nrow(.x), sample_per_class))) |>
  ungroup()

# Define lightweight training parameters
formula_m1 <- as.formula(paste("mode ~", paste(movement_features, collapse = " + ")))
formula_m2 <- as.formula(paste("mode ~", paste(context_features, collapse = " + ")))

# Train models directly with rpart to avoid caret's extra tuning overhead
model_movement <- rpart::rpart(formula_m1, data = train_set, method = "class", control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0.01, maxdepth = 5))
model_context <- rpart::rpart(formula_m2, data = train_set, method = "class", control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0.01, maxdepth = 5))

# Evaluate both models on the independent test set
predictions_m1 <- predict(model_movement, test_set, type = "class")
predictions_m2 <- predict(model_context, test_set, type = "class")

confusion_matrix_m1 <- confusionMatrix(predictions_m1, test_set$mode)
confusion_matrix_m2 <- confusionMatrix(predictions_m2, test_set$mode)

# Print overall accuracy metrics to console for comparison
cat("--- Baseline Model Accuracy (Movement Only) ---\n")
print(confusion_matrix_m1$overall["Accuracy"])

cat("--- Enhanced Model Accuracy (Movement + Context) ---\n")
print(confusion_matrix_m2$overall["Accuracy"])
```
